lead.label: 4a
lead.why: Abstract: 'Synthetic macamide 4a was the most active (IC50 = 0.009 +/- 0.001 uM) compared to the C87 (control).'

reactions.conditions: General procedure 3.4: alcohol (1.0 eq) in dry CH2Cl2, Et3N (1.2 eq), 0 C, acid chloride added dropwise, 10 min; 10% HCl workup; flash chromatography Hex-AcOEt 6:1; 80% yield (0.46 mmol scale).
reactions.source: Main text sections 2 (p. 5-7, 4a made 'as for 2g, reacting the acid chloride with an alcohol'), 3.4 general procedure, 3.7 spectroscopic data for 4a

notes: Printed name of 4a ends in '-1-olate' (a naming error in the paper; the compound is the ester, 1-(3,5-dimethylphenyl)ethyl linoleate, as the text says 'reacting the acid chloride with an alcohol'); OPSIN will likely fail or disagree on the printed name, the SMILES is the ester. Acid chloride and alcohol are used from commercial sources ('reagents purchased from commercial sources and used without prior purification'); no preparation of the acid chloride is described. Stereo: 9Z,12Z as printed. Racemic alcohol (no stereo stated). The 4a NMR listing in the paper looks copy-pasted from 3m (amide NH signal) but that does not affect the transcription.
